discovery.notes: Project is greenfield — no code in fabro.report repo yet. Entities below were elicited and confirmed through the initialize conversation with Bryan, cross-referenced against bun.report (template) and the fabro monorepo (domain context).

confirmed_entities.name: Report
confirmed_entities.annotation: The upload event and its public identity. Fields: ID, URL, upload timestamp, bundle size, optional reporter message, Fabro version, arbitrary key/value metadata, retention deadline (default 30d). Delete capability is tied to URL possession.

confirmed_entities.name: Debug Bundle
confirmed_entities.annotation: Compressed tarball produced by `fabro debug`. Stored in S3, never served publicly. Payload structure is out of scope for this library — owned by the `fabro debug` command in the main Fabro repo.

confirmed_entities.name: Reporter
confirmed_entities.annotation: Whoever ran `fabro report`. No identity, no login. Identified only by Fabro version metadata captured at upload.

confirmed_entities.name: Triager
confirmed_entities.annotation: Fabro team members (Bryan + team) who retrieve bundles for bug investigation. Access bundles via direct S3 access using their own credentials. Never interact with the intake service itself.

confirmed_entities.name: Report Metadata Page
confirmed_entities.annotation: The minimal landing page at the returned URL. Shows ID / upload timestamp / bundle size and a delete button. Does NOT expose bundle contents — that security decision is deliberate.

context.product_summary: fabro.report is a debug-bundle intake service for users of the Fabro product (an AI workflow orchestration platform at ~/p/fabro-sh/fabro). Users run `fabro report`, which uploads a compressed tarball to S3 and returns a URL. The Fabro team triages bugs by retrieving bundles directly from S3.
context.template_reference: ~/p/oven-sh/bun.report — stated as a shape template, but scope is narrower: no symbolication, no Sentry integration, no bundle rendering, no feedback collection. Only the intake + secret-URL pattern is borrowed.
context.parent_product: ~/p/fabro-sh/fabro — Rust monorepo, AI-powered workflow orchestration, workflows defined as Graphviz graphs.
context.security_model: Capability URLs — knowledge of the URL grants the ability to view metadata and delete the report. No authentication on the public surface.
context.dedup: Disabled by design — bundles expire anyway.
context.headless_caveat: User described this as 'headless' but confirmed a minimal 1-page metadata receipt exists at each Report URL. Effectively near-headless, not literally.
